name: AakashNet (Photonics Odyssey)
tagline: Satellite broadband for India designed as sovereign national infrastructure: low-cost phased-array terminals linked to a laser-meshed LEO constellation.
problem: More than 700 million people in India are offline; fiber and towers are impractical in remote terrain, and relying on foreign satellite networks raises sovereignty and security concerns.
solution: A concept for an indigenous LEO network with laser inter-satellite links and a mass-producible phased-array user terminal (about 1,280 elements, Ku/Ka band, electronic beam steering), with RF link budgets modeled in MATLAB and OpenEMS and a lightweight browser dashboard that visualizes coverage, beam switching and throughput.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the project that 'captures our hearts'.
The stake is specific and enormous: helping connect more than 700 million people without broadband.
Designed around national constraints rather than a generic constellation: a terminal cost cap, local manufacturing and encrypted links for public services and defense.
Inverts the commercial framing of the LEO challenge (private service → public infrastructure), which makes a concept entry memorable without a working product.
Its only listed NASA resource is the image and video library, so the award rewarded stakes and framing more than data depth.

lessons: A concept can win an inspiration award when the stake is huge, specific and tied to one country's constraints.
Flip the challenge's default framing to stand out in a popular challenge.
Inspiration lanes weigh stakes over data depth; data-heavy awards will not.

sources.note: Team-written concept, terminal design, constraints, tools, AI-use disclosure and data.
